title: The Friendship of Horses
paragraphs: On a farm near my home two horses are kept. From a distance they look no different from any others. But when you come closer you notice something remarkable: one of them is blind. His owner could not bear to part with him and built him a safe, comfortable stall. That alone is an astonishing act of kindness.

If you approach the horses you will hear a little bell. The sound comes from the other horse — a small, sound animal whose bridle carries a bell — so that the blind horse can tell where he is and follow.

Watch the two friends carefully and you will see that the horse with the bell always checks where the blind one is; and the blind horse, for his part, listens for the bell and slowly follows his sound companion.
Every evening, as the horse with the bell returns to the stall, he pauses now and then and looks back to make sure his blind friend is close enough to hear the chime.
The Lord does not leave us alone in hard times; when we need help He sends it through a human hand. And sometimes it falls to us to be that helper.

title: Meddling in Others' Lives
paragraphs: May God never leave anyone so idle that they meddle in other people's lives!
Unasked advice is not help but a burden. To interfere in another's life under the name of «kindness» often does harm.

title: A Pair of Boots
paragraphs: One day a teacher asked her pupils to write a story on any subject they chose, and promised to give «a pair of boots» to whoever wrote the finest one. All the pupils wrote their stories and handed them in.
The teacher read the stories one by one and liked them all. She found it hard to pick the best. After thinking it over she decided to settle the winner by drawing lots.

Each pupil wrote a name on a slip of paper, folded it, and dropped it into a box on the teacher's desk. When the slips had been mixed, she drew one out and called aloud: «Amina!» The whole class burst into applause.
The pupil named Amina had won the draw. Clutching the boots tightly to her chest in joy, the little girl could not hold back her tears.
That evening, when she reached home, the teacher began tearfully to tell her husband what had happened in class. Her husband said:
— Well, what a fine solution you found — why are you crying?
The teacher went on:
— You see, not one pupil wrote his own name — every slip bore only the name of Amina, the poorest child in the class. The whole class had wanted her alone to win those boots.
The finest victory is to put another's joy above your own. An entire class freely gave up its chance for one poor friend.

title: A Handful of Roasted Chickpeas
paragraphs: A child went with his mother into a shop that sold snacks. He kept pleading, «I want roasted chickpeas.» Seeing that the mother was reluctant, the shopkeeper felt sorry for the boy:
— Come, little one, take a handful yourself.
— No — I'll take them only if you give them, — the boy objected.
The shopkeeper gave him a full handful of roasted chickpeas and asked:
— Why didn't you take them yourself? Why did you want me to give them?
— Because your hand is bigger, — the boy smiled.
— Mashallah, what a clever little one you are, — said the shopkeeper, smiling too.
Whom you ask from sometimes matters more than what you ask for. When the giving hand is different, the portion is different too.

title: A Glass of Milk
paragraphs: A poor boy who was trying to pay for his schooling by going door to door selling small wares one day found himself without a penny and fiercely hungry. He resolved that at the next door he would ask the householder for something to eat. And so he did. He came to the next house and knocked. But when a beautiful woman opened the door he lost his nerve and asked for water instead of food. The woman sensed that the boy was hungry and brought him a glass of milk instead of water. When he had drunk the milk slowly he asked how much he owed her. The woman answered:
— You owe me nothing, — she said, and added: — My mother brought us up to «do kindness without seeking return.»
Howard Kelly was a little overcome and could only say:
— I thank you from the heart.
As he left the house he felt stronger in body, and also felt his faith in God and in humanity grow firmer.

Years passed. One day that same woman fell gravely ill. The local doctors could find no remedy for her affliction. At last, at a loss, they sent her to a great city so that specialists might search out the cause of this rare disease.

Dr Howard Kelly was called into the consultation. The moment he heard which town the patient had come from, his eyes seemed to fill with light. He rose at once and went to the ward where she had been placed. He knew her the instant he saw her: this was the woman who in his childhood had saved him from hunger with a glass of milk and strengthened the love of God in his heart.
From that day the doctor took the woman under his care and resolved to do everything in his power to heal her.
After a long struggle the disease was defeated and the woman recovered her health. The time came for her to leave the hospital and go home.

Dr Kelly asked the accounts office for the bill setting out the cost of treatment. He took the bill, wrote something in the margin, and had it sent to the woman's ward. She took it up in agitation and, seeing the sum, grew despondent, certain she could never pay it. She thought she would have to labour all her life to clear that debt.
Suddenly a sentence in the margin caught her eye:
«Paid in full with a glass of milk.» Signed: Dr Howard Kelly.
Kindness done without hope of return is never lost; it is written on an unseen ledger and, when the time comes — when you least expect it — is given back.

title: Everyone Is the Same Here
paragraphs: A young man newly appointed head of the district municipality decided to walk about and acquaint himself with how things stood. After touring the area alone he stepped into a teahouse on a side street and ordered himself some tea.
Just then a boy of twelve or thirteen said:
— Uncle, shall I polish your shoes?
Though his shoes were already polished, so as not to hurt the boy's feelings he said:
— All right, come and polish them. If you do it well I'll give you twice whatever you ask, — and the boy answered:
— I polish the same way for everyone.
The official said:
— How do you mean?
The boy replied:

— Our teacher told us: «Children, whatever work you do, do it the same for everyone; make no distinctions.» And I am going to buy medicine for my sick mother with this money. If I served you differently, that medicine would bring her no healing!

The young official had been given one of the most important lessons of his life. He was deeply moved and gave the boy the largest note in his pocket, and his own card as well. He promised to take an interest in this fatherless child who both studied and tried to care for his sick mother.
He also went to see the teacher who had instilled that honesty in the boy and thanked him specially.
So as never to forget what he had heard from the shoe-shine boy, and always to apply it in his work, he had the words «Everyone is the same here» written on the back of the nameplate on his desk.
Hard though it was, he always tried to practise it in his work.
Treat a person the same not for the position he holds, but because he is a human being. Society is changed by those who choose what is right in small moments.

title: Gossip
paragraphs: A sharp-tongued, discourteous man was summoned before the village elder, accused of spreading gossip.
— It was only a joke, just a joke, — he said, denying the charge. — Others misunderstood my words; I am not to blame!
But the one who had been gossiped about stood firm:
— You stained my good name. I demand justice.
As he was pressed harder the guilty man drew back:
— I take back everything I said; I beg to be forgiven.
The elder listened in silence. He thought to himself: «This man has not yet grasped the weight of what he did. Time will pass and he will repeat the same offence.» Then he said to him:

— Go to the market square and bring a pillow stuffed with bird feathers. Cut it open and scatter the feathers about. Then gather every last feather and bring them to me. If you cannot, there will be no forgiveness.

The man accepted the elder's condition reluctantly. Thinking, «The old man has lost his mind,» he brought the pillow to the square and cut it open. One puff of wind scattered the feathers to every side. He ran now right, now left, chasing after them; yet however hard he tried, in the end only a few feathers remained in his hand.
Head bowed, he returned to the elder:
— I could not gather the rest.
Then he drew a deep sigh:
— Just like the words I spread. I can never take them back either.
A word once set loose is like a feather given to the wind — it cannot be gathered again. Therefore keep clear of gossip.

title: I Want a Friend
paragraphs: I want neither goods nor property —
I want a true friend.
What estate has ever recited a prayer of mercy for its dead owner?
I want a friend who will pray for mercy upon me.
Neither goods nor property — for a human being the true wealth is a loyal friend. A friend who will pray for mercy after you are gone is worth more than any estate.

title: Those You Should Not Befriend
paragraphs: — Do not befriend the arrogant! He knows no courtesy, no mood, no heart; you will be hurt.
— Do not befriend the one who thinks himself very clever! He talks much, talks empty, talks little of worth; you will be hurt.
— Do not befriend the base! He knows no honour, no heart, no friend; you will be hurt.
From friendship with the arrogant, the self-satisfied, and the base, only regret remains. Choose your friend by the heart.

title: Know Your Friend
paragraphs: If you wish to know your friend — see him in hardship, see him in straits, see him in a quarrel; and still, touch his interest, and see him then.
A friend is known in hardship, in straits, and in the trial of self-interest. In easy days everyone is a friend; true friendship is revealed by difficulty.

title: Go, but Come Again
paragraphs: Among Ottoman customs: hosts who wished their guests to come again would set the guests' shoes at the door with the toes pointed toward the house. Thus when a guest left he seemed almost to walk out backwards — and that meant «go, but come again.»
A delicate gesture can carry great kindness. The regard shown to a person is often seen in the smallest details.

title: Permission or Apology
paragraphs: There is a saying attributed to Rear Admiral Grace Hopper: «It is easier to ask forgiveness than permission.»
The phrase is used to mean: «Do not ask leave beforehand to do a thing — do it, and if someone is displeased afterward, apologize.»
Sometimes waiting for permission is to let opportunity slip away. Do what you know to be right; apologize later if you must.

Imagine a company with an obvious problem that slows the work. Say each week the same data is copied by hand into several different tables, and hours go into it. One employee sees that a simple automation could solve it.

If he first tried at length to obtain permission, the matter might pass from one manager to another, weeks of waiting might follow, and the chance be lost. Seeing that the risk is small, the employee builds a separate trial system without harming existing data, automates the process, and shows the result. If the system succeeds, everyone sees its benefit. Should anyone be displeased that the procedure was not agreed in advance, the employee can say: «I ran a trial to speed the process. If I broke a rule, I apologize.»

The main idea here is not «ignore the rules.» The point is that in cases where the outcome can be reversed, the danger is slight, and the benefit is clear, waiting endlessly for leave can kill initiative. Sometimes it is righter to act with responsibility and show the result than to wait forever for approval.

title: A Compliment
paragraphs: Maria lived with her mother in a small flat in New York. She worked as a secretary in a large firm; her life was thoroughly dull and ordinary.
At work no one paid her any attention...
One morning on her way to work Maria noticed that a new hat shop had opened on the street. Curious, she went inside.
In the shop there were a mother with a little girl, and another customer looking for a hat. Maria tried on several. She liked one very much and set it on her head. The hat suited her wonderfully.
The little girl watching Maria called out: «Mama, look how beautiful that lady looks in the hat!»
The mother turned to Maria:
— Madam, that hat suits you beautifully, — she said.
The other customer came nearer too: «Madam, you look wonderful in that hat!»
Maria went to the mirror and looked at herself.
For the first time in her life she liked the reflection she saw so much. She looked splendid.
Smiling, she went to the till and paid for the hat.

When she stepped outside a wholly new world opened before her... She had never seen how lovely the colours of the flowers were. The sweet smell of clean air, the sound of cars and people, were like a harmonious melody...
She felt very beautiful.
When she reached the office building the guard opened the door and said «good morning.»
Those in the lift asked which floor she wanted; someone pressed the button for her.
All day the people in the office looked at her with admiration, said how lovely she looked that day — as if they were seeing her for the first time.
Her manager invited her to lunch to ask her opinion on a new piece of work.
When that magical working day ended Maria was still smiling. She thought of the miraculous day she had lived and how her life had changed in an instant. All thanks to the new hat...
She took a taxi home. When she arrived her mother opened the door and, seeing Maria, stood amazed: «Maria, how beautiful you look! Your eyes are shining as they did in childhood!» she said.
— Yes, Mother, it is all thanks to my new hat. I have had an astonishing day!
— Which hat? — her mother asked in confusion.

Maria grew uneasy. The expression on her face suddenly changed. She touched her head and saw that the hat that had changed her life was not there. She did not remember taking it when she got into the taxi. Perhaps she had forgotten it at lunch? Working with such zest in the office she had not even touched the hat. She recalled the shop: how she had first seen the hat, how she had put it on, the admiration of those around her, how she had taken it and gone to the till, taken out her purse and laid the hat on the counter...
But!
She also remembered how, in her excitement, she had left the hat on the counter and walked out bareheaded, her eyes shining...
What had made Maria happy all day were the thoughts and feelings themselves that she had lived through...
A person who lives in happiness sheds a bright light upon those around. Ordinary things look magical, darkness clears, the zest for living grows stronger.
One kind word can change a person's whole world. Happiness is not in an outward object, but within the person and in the attention shown to them.

title: How We Treat People
paragraphs: Let your way with people be like your way with fire:
do not stand too far off, lest you freeze;
do not come too near, lest you burn.
Saadi Shirazi
Keep measure in your dealings with people: neither draw so far away that you grow cold, nor come so close that you are burned.

title: Humanity
paragraphs: For years he studied and toiled, and at last the day of the examination that would decide his fate arrived... His father, Kazim, was a demanding man; he always took a close interest in his son's lessons and was sure the boy would succeed in that exam...

Kamal entered the building and found the classroom where he was to sit the exam. When the question and answer sheets were handed out he was nervous, yet once the exam began he grew quite calm... He answered the questions easily and was wholly sure his answers were right... Half an hour remained until the end. He was so sure of himself...
Suddenly he fixed his eyes intently on the classroom window. Whatever he saw, without a thought he sprang up and ran for the door...
— Come back! Or the exam will be cancelled and a whole year will be lost, my son, — called the teacher invigilating. But he did not stop; he ran out through the back door of the building...

Hearing what had happened, his father first scolded Kamal when he came home a few hours later, then even struck him across the face. Kazim was deeply distressed. Though he asked why his son had left the classroom and abandoned the exam unfinished, Kamal kept silent, knowing his father would only grow angrier... If he had told him, he would not have understood...
All that year Kazim reproached and blamed his son without cease. Though Kamal was hurt by this, he said nothing; he lowered his head and kept to his studies.

The next year he sat the exam again and was admitted to the faculty of medicine... He became a very fine doctor. Though he had lived for many years in the city, he asked of his own will to be posted to a remote village hospital. After a year of work there his family came to visit his home... The matter of the exam between him and his father had long been forgotten...

On a snowy, cold evening Kamal's home telephone rang. The caller said there was a patient in one of the nearby villages. As he took his bag and set out, his father Kazim would not leave his son alone on the mountain roads and decided to go with him. Under a hard blizzard they walked about an hour and reached that village. They found the house and knocked. An elderly man opened the door, said his wife was ill, and invited the doctor in with his father...

Kamal examined the patient and prescribed the needed treatment. The elderly woman thanked the doctor and said in a trembling voice: «In this cold you have been the remedy for our trouble, my son. Without good people like you, what would this world be? To be human is no easy thing... Listen.»

«Years ago I had gone into the city. Suddenly in the middle of the road I grew very ill; I was seized with sharp pain. There was no one about; the streets were empty. As it happened, that day there was an examination. Before five minutes had passed a young man came up to me in agitation. In that heat he got me to the hospital in half an hour. I was pregnant and shook with fear that something might happen to my child. The doctor in admissions said that if I had been ten minutes later I might have died... That day my son was born.

I learned the name of the boy who had brought me to the hospital — he said he was Kamal. He told me: I was in an exam; looking out of the window I saw you, and when I understood you were alone I left the classroom and came to help. Though I lost a year by giving up the exam, I never regretted it.

I named my son Kamal. I raised him on the story of that merciful young man and constantly counselled him to become a person like Kamal. Now he is a teacher... He tries first of all to bring his pupils up as human beings... Ah, if only I could find that young man and receive his blessing... Anyone can become a doctor, a teacher, an engineer. The hardest thing in this world is to be a human being... What a fine person that youth was. He did not leave me alone in the middle of the road.» Hearing this, Dr Kamal said: «It is blessed, Mother; do not worry...»

His father Kazim was moved to tears, yet did not wish to show them. But as they left the house the tears wet his cheeks. Even after they set out on the road Kazim's tears did not stop. In a trembling voice he said «Kamal, my son,» but a sob choked him and he could not finish.
One may have a profession; the true hard thing is to be human. The mercy a young man showed in time becomes a good that lasts for generations.
